claim_scope_change: S6 now asks: given the same 94-example training budget from the fixed S5 candidate pool, does priority-v1 selection generalize better than uniform selection on a separate, identically supervised, component-disjoint evaluation population?

design.eval_source: fresh S5 pool under a frozen seed with a HELD-OUT opening partition (openings the training pool never played); separate S#### ids are not assumed to imply independence
design.freeze: D_EVAL (0,0,1) + one E_COMMON; source/normalization/dataset/protocol hashes pinned into the campaign identity
design.if_insufficient: fail closed and enlarge the pool without examining any target values
design.joint_component_check: union-find over canonical record identities across the training corpus and the evaluation source; every evaluation candidate whose joint component contains any PRIORITY or UNIFORM training member is rejected
design.labels: exactly the required 400k-node search_deep_cp labels, bought with the same pinned analyze binary/net identity as the training TargetSpec
design.pre_smoke_assertion: record ids AND joint provenance components disjoint from the union of the arms
design.selection: 200 records by deterministic hash order: lowest sha256(eval_selection_seed, record_id)

reason: the corrected campaign's corpus cannot supply a leakage-safe internal evaluation slice: the 938-record S5 pool collapses to 12 transposition components (largest 145 records) and the 182 unique selected arm records touch all 12, so no component-disjoint evaluation population exists inside the pool
title: independent evaluation population
